common_mistakes: Submitting the building permit without a separate scaffold or sidewalk protection approval when the scaffold will sit in the public right-of-way
Treating lintel replacement as minor repair — once you replace a masonry lintel, plan review and structural details are often required
Starting demolition before the permit is issued and posted on site

Submitting permit application without verifying current Philadelphia contractor registration status — an expired or lapsed city registration will block your application silently. Verify your registration is current BEFORE submitting.

pro_tips: Have a structural repair sketch or engineer's detail ready before opening the portal — lintel replacement jobs move much faster when the reviewer can see bearing, support, and repair details up front.
Check your Philadelphia contractor registration renewal date before starting any permit application — registration lapses are one of the most avoidable rejection reasons.
If the scaffold touches the sidewalk, coordinate the sidewalk protection and building permit together so you do not get stuck waiting on one approval while the other is ready.
For a $140,000 commercial facade job, expect plan review rather than EZ processing; submitting a clean plan set the first time saves weeks.
